record.context_brief: Tightness of the binary Varshamov-Gilbert bound
record.original_question: For binary codes, is the Varshamov-Gilbert bound actually tight?

evidence.quote: Open Question 11.2. Is the VG bound tight for q = 2? It is not for q > 49 thanks to AG codes and the TVZ bound [72].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For positive integers $n$ and $d$, let $A_2(n,d)$ denote the maximum size of a binary code of length $n$ and minimum Hamming distance at least $d$; that is, the largest cardinality of a subset $C\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$ such that any two distinct $x,y\in C$ differ in at least $d$ coordinates. For $0<\delta<1/2$, define the asymptotic rate function
$$R(\delta)=\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n}\log_2 A_2(n,\lfloor \delta n\rfloor).$$
Let $H_2(\delta)=-\delta\log_2\delta-(1-\delta)\log_2(1-\delta)$ denote the binary entropy function. The (binary) Gilbert–Varshamov bound asserts that $R(\delta)\geq 1-H_2(\delta)$ for all $\delta\in(0,1/2)$.

Decide whether the Gilbert–Varshamov bound is asymptotically tight in the binary case: is it true that
$$R(\delta)=1-H_2(\delta)\quad\text{for all }\delta\in(0,1/2)\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: The tightness of the binary Gilbert–Varshamov bound is a long-standing open problem in coding theory. For alphabets of size q ≥ 49, the Tsfasman–Vlăduț–Zink bound from algebraic-geometry codes improves on Gilbert–Varshamov, but no asymptotic improvement is known for binary codes, and it remains a conjecture (often attributed to Goppa) that the bound is asymptotically tight in the binary case. Recent expository sources (MIT open-problems notes; CMU lecture notes; surveys) continue to list this as open.

status_evidence.title: Problem 7.1: Gilbert-Varshamov Bound (MIT 18.S096)
status_evidence.snippet: Determining the largest rate possible for binary codes of given relative distance is a fundamental open problem; whether the Gilbert–Varshamov bound is tight is open.
status_evidence.claim: The tightness of the binary GV bound is listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Notes 2: Gilbert–Varshamov bound (CMU Spring 2010)
status_evidence.snippet: The popular conjecture (attributed to Goppa) is that the GV bound on rate is asymptotically tight for binary codes, though there is no strong evidence either way.
status_evidence.claim: It is a conjecture, not a theorem, that the binary GV bound is tight.

status_evidence.title: Asymptotic Improvement of the Gilbert–Varshamov Bound
status_evidence.snippet: Improvements over GV via algebraic-geometry codes are known only for q ≥ 49; no asymptotic improvement is known for binary codes.
status_evidence.claim: No asymptotic improvement of the binary GV bound is known.
